source_verification: Every recorded execution-source hash in both runs matches the corresponding committed file at 9829512. Subsequent edits only add a counterexample/metadata test and clarify future output metadata; the numerical records are preserved.
configuration: Single-edge exchanges only. Union uses global six plus group-diverse six, deduplicates and fills to twelve. The equal-cap control is global twelve, not global six. All use three removals and an eight-step limit.

query_checks.pilot: Twenty reused validation queries from PubMed training seed 42, including the diagnosed failure.
query_checks.additional: One hundred validation queries from training seed 43, fifty per class, with zero overlap with the twenty query keys excluded from the reference run.
query_checks.per_variant_caps: Each trace was checked against its actual addition count, not only the largest study-wide cap. All nonempty exchange-size histograms contain only single exchanges.

pilot.diagnosed_case: Union restores sufficiency for query [15167,19061] at budget five. Simply doubling the old diverse-only pool does not restore it. Global six and global twelve also restore it.

additional_validation.continuous_metrics: Differences are small and mixed across budgets. Binary ties do not imply identical supports or continuous fidelity; complete paired differences are in each run.

cost: Union generally uses roughly twice as many evaluated proposals as the smaller six-addition pool. Its maximum per-step count matches global twelve, but actual totals and runtime vary with trajectories. Search timing excludes shared partition construction, query grouping, saliency initialization, and final metric reporting; no end-to-end speed claim is made.
metadata_caveat: The archived v1 args dictionary inherited unused pair_swaps/mixed_swaps flags from the reference benchmark. The executed source, variant_configuration, and recorded exchange-size histograms establish that these runs used single-edge search only. The v2 writer separates reference_args from explicit executed-study arguments; no measurements were rewritten.
interpretation: Coverage union repairs an identifiable shortlist failure but shows no independent binary-fidelity advantage over the equal-cap global or nonspectral controls on the additional validation queries. It is not selected as a final method or a new coarsening contribution.
decision: Retain the optional implementation and negative/neutral records. Do not continue choosing score or grouping seeds to improve these queries. Further method work should investigate whether coarse computation itself can offer a useful, controlled advantage over exact local computation, rather than presenting candidate diversity as established value.
limitations: This is one dataset with two trained checkpoints and validation, not final held-out testing. Multiple budgets on a query are dependent. Same-state candidate inclusion is not a guarantee of terminal search dominance.
manuscript: Unchanged this turn; empirical LaTeX numbers remain frozen.
